10.14.8.en: "When the wicked cometh, then cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach" (Prov 18:3).

10.14.9.en: "Do not exalt yourself lest you fall, and bring dishonor upon yourself" (Sir 1:38).

10.14.10.en: "The lot of the lying man is dishonor, and his shame is with him continually" (Sir 20:28).

10.14.11.en: "A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss at his disgrace" (Sir 22:1).

10.14.12.en: "As they were increased, so they sinned against me: therefore will I change their glory into shame" (Hos 4:7).

10.14.13.en: "For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature" (Rom 1:26).

10.14.14.en: * Besides the inherited (ancestral) evils, I added evils of my own... The sin of Adam, without doubt, does not allow a man to look upward with boldness, nor to glorify himself. Therefore Job says: "I am full of confusion."

10.14.15.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem. * Yes, for "woe" is for the wicked, and for the righteous "sorrow"; eternal punishment overtakes the sinner who perishes, while each one of the elect is purified by the pains of temporary sorrow...

10.14.16.en: But if we overlook for a time the sin of our first father, we find ourselves hunted by the evil habit of pride.

10.14.17.en: It often happens that through the virtues granted him, man is puffed up with boldness and self-righteousness, but through the wonderful dispensation of divine providence it is permitted that certain opposing things be placed before his eyes into which some fall...

10.14.18.en: When the saint sees what happens to his fellows, a cry comes forth from him personally concerning the dangers to which we are exposed.

10.14.19.en: In this way, when we read of the lament of a certain person, we learn to grieve over what is within ourselves.

10.14.20.en: Now when pride rises in the mind, the wounded feeling of love for the heights leaves us, but when grace comes upon us from above, it immediately urges us to long for it with tears.

10.14.22.en: * Rightly he says: "If I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head, for I am full of confusion" [15]. The righteous man knows his weakness...

10.14.23.en: The wise man is moved to recognize them, and the fool does not do so.

10.14.24.en: Truly the wise man is moved toward repentance and remembers his faults, and the ignorant man delights in them.

10.14.25.en: The wise man is he who accuses himself (Prov 18:17), but the wicked man is the one who defends himself.

10.14.26.en: The righteous man wishes to precede his accuser in accusing himself of his sins, but the wicked man wishes to silence him.

10.14.27.en: One hastens from the beginning to speak of his faults, and the other tries to accuse others with his talkative speech so that his sins may not be exposed.

10.14.28.en: St. Ambrose. In one of the Festal Letters, St. Athanasius the Apostolic depicts for us the dishonor that comes upon the human soul because of sin, while the righteous, who have pure hearts, enjoy glory, that is, the glory of seeing God.

10.14.29.en: * We say that the wicked are dead, but not in a life of devotion against sin, nor do they, like the saints, bear death in their bodies; rather they bury the soul in sins and follies, so that the soul draws near to death. And as they feed it with deadly pleasures, their souls are like young vultures hovering over the corpses of the dead. The Law declared this when it commanded, in symbolic form, not to eat vultures and all the birds that feed on carrion (Lev 11:13).

10.14.30.en: These kill the soul with lusts, and say nothing but "let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die" (Isa 22:13).

10.14.31.en: And the prophet described the fruit gathered by such as these who plunge into pleasures, saying: "And it was revealed in mine ears by the LORD of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die" (Isa 22:14).

10.14.32.en: Yes, even while they live they are in shame, for they reckon their belly as their god, and when they die they are tormented, because they boasted of such a death.

10.14.33.en: Paul also bears witness to this result, saying: "Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them" (1 Cor 6:13).

10.14.34.en: And the divine Word declares concerning these that the death of the wicked is evil, and those who hate the righteous do wrong (Ps 34:21), for the wicked inherit bitter fire and destroying darkness.

10.14.35.en: But the saints and those who practice virtue truly have mortified their members which are upon the earth: fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence (Col 3:5). So there is fulfilled in them, because of this purity and undefiledness, the promise of our Savior: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God" (Mt 5:8).

10.15.0.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic. "For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me" [16]!

10.15.1.en: As though he had become prey in the mouth of a lion, with no refuge and no escape, and no mercy or compassion! One translation reads: "If I am proud and haughty like a lion, You hunt me."

10.15.2.en: * Man is rightly likened to a lion, for it is a royal beast (Gen 28:8-9). Moreover the righteous man, as he preserves in himself the dignity of the image (of God), is dreadful to his adversaries. It is said of this in the book of Proverbs: [The righteous are bold as a lion] (cf. Prov 28:1). But if he sinks down to covetousness, as his enemies urge him to do, at that very moment he is "hunted like a lion for slaughter." He becomes an object of mockery to those who were tracking him, and is like the lion which, as soon as it falls into their enticement, they hunt down.

10.15.3.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem. "Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me."

10.16.1.en: What multiplied Job's calamity was that he felt God's wrath increasing, which made the trial more bitter and heavy. God does not lack witnesses against Job; if one witness fails, a new witness stands in his place. Since the word "witnesses" in Greek means "martyrs," it is as though those who bear witness to God, to His love, His divine providence, and His work of salvation even unto death, become witnesses against those who doubt God's providence and murmur against Him. The appearance of these holy witnesses condemns us, so that we have no argument or justification for our sinful conduct, and Job expressed this by saying: "and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me."

10.16.2.en: "Changes and war are against me." One translation reads: "Your armies take turns against me."

10.16.3.en: * God's witnesses are those who bear witness by the practice of holy works... also those who suffer for the truth. In the Greek tongue "martyrs" are "witnesses." The Lord says through John by the voice of the angel: [even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful witness, who was slain among you] (Rev 2:13).

10.16.4.en: Now the Lord renews His witnesses against us when He multiplies the lives of the elect, so that they challenge our evil with the aim of persuading and teaching us... All that they do is contrary to our evil. Therefore the word of truth is called "the adversary," as the Mediator says in the Gospel: "Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him" (Mt 5:25). And the sons of perdition say in their persecutions concerning the Savior Himself: "He is clearly against our doings," and after that: [his life is not like other men's] (Wis 2:12, 15). Thus God renews His witnesses against us, to show that the good works which we neglect are practiced by others, to rebuke us...

10.16.5.en: It was fitting to add: "and increasest thine indignation upon me"... as Peter testified, saying: "For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?" (1 Pet 4:17). Therefore when Almighty God renews His witnesses against us He "increases His indignation" as is fitting, for He sets the lives of the righteous before our eyes, and shows with what severity He will strike our stubbornness while we practice sin, at the judgment.

10.17.0.en: 18 "Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me! 19 I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave. 20 Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little, 21 Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death; 22 A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness."

10.17.1.en: The writings of the early Church and its concepts in its worship, asceticism, canons, and every aspect of its life bore a biblical eschatological stamp. The doctrine of the life to come was not merely a principal element of faith, but the very core of the faith itself! The early Church, as a truly biblical Church, was an eschatological Church; it set its heart in heaven, to live as an ambassador of the heavenly Christ, drawing the world toward heaven and bringing it into the life of Paradise, that it might await in hope the fullness of eternal glory and the heavenly inheritance.

10.17.2.en: As for the view of Old Testament believers toward death, it is expressed in what is found in the Book of Wisdom: [For God created man for incorruption, and made him an image of His own divine self, but through the devil's envy death entered the world] (Wis 2:23, 24). God did not create death, and therefore through righteousness man obtains immortality: [For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living. For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthful; and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of death upon the earth: for righteousness is immortal] (Wis 1:13-15). As it is also said: [For to know thy power is the root of immortality] (Wis 15:3).

10.17.3.en: The believing fathers in the Old Testament looked upon death as being gathered or sleeping with their fathers (Gen 25:8; 47:30), and they feared only going down to Sheol in sorrow (Gen 27:35). They counted death in a good old age a blessing (Gen 15:15; 25:8), while the cutting off of a man from the land of the living in the prime of his youth was a fearful thing (Isa 38:10).

10.17.4.en: Nevertheless the Jews' view of death differed from one person to another, and Alfred Edersheim presented to us a comparison between two Jewish leaders in their view of death.

10.17.5.en: The first leader is Rabbi Jochanan ben Saccai. It is told of him in the Talmud that his disciples came to him as he lay on his deathbed, and he burst into tears. They were amazed at this, and asked how it was that "the light of Israel, the pillar of the true Temple," should be betrayed in this way by signs of fear. The Rabbi answered them: "If I were being brought before an earthly king who lives today and dies tomorrow, whose wrath and chains are not eternal, and whose pronouncing of the sentence of death is not eternal death, and with whom one can easily enter into dialogue or buy him with money, I would be terrified at this and weep; how much more is my condition, now that I have drawn near to stand before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, who lives and abides forever, whose chains are everlasting chains, and whose sentence of death is an eternal sentence, whom I cannot converse with by words nor bribe with money! And it does not stop at this, but before me are two ways: one toward Paradise and the other toward Gehenna, and I do not know to which of the two ways I shall go: whether to Paradise or to Gehenna; how then should I not shed tears?"

10.17.6.en: The second example is R. Jehudah, who is called the Saint, for when he died he raised his hands toward heaven, affirming that not one of his ten fingers had broken the Law of God!

10.17.7.en: The first is utterly without hope, living in great despair and fearing the meeting with God, in spite of his position as head of the greatest assembly among the Jews, and the second, in great pride and certainty, thinks that he will surely enjoy Paradise, because he did not break any commandment with any of his fingers. Two completely extreme pictures: one crushed by despair, the other crushed by pride!

10.17.8.en: "Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb?"

10.17.9.en: "Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!" [18]

10.17.10.en: Job repeats the same desire that he had already declared in an earlier discourse (Job 3:11).

10.17.11.en: Again Job longed to have been stifled in the womb, not to come out into the world, and for no one to see him.

10.17.12.en: Perhaps Job felt that he had become a byword and a mockery to all who looked at him, so he wished that he had never seen anyone at all, and that no one had seen him.

10.18.0.en: "I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave" [19].

10.18.1.en: Just as he who sets his heart on temporal life sins, so he who despairs of life and longs for death out of despair sins. The first loves the world and the creature more than its Creator, and the second slights God's plan for him.

10.19.0.en: "Cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort (smile) a little" [20].

10.19.1.en: He asks God to cease from discipline so that he may catch his breath and rest a little.

10.19.2.en: Job knows that the days of man are few, so in this little time he asks for some rest, even if only from time to time.

10.19.3.en: * Solomon said: "But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity" (Eccl 11:8). Again he wrote: [Whatever you take in hand, remember your end, and you will never sin]. Therefore when sin tempts the mind, the soul should perceive the purpose of its delight, lest sin hasten it to certain death, since it is clear that mortal life quickly comes to an end.

10.19.5.en: * O sons of Adam, over whom death has reigned, think of death, and remember life, and do not transgress the commandment like your first father.

10.19.6.en: O kings crowned with crowns, remember death, which will take away the crowns placed on your heads; it will be king over you until the time comes when you rise for judgment.

10.19.7.en: O you who are haughty and proud and arrogant, remember death, which will shatter your haughtiness, and loosen your limbs, and undo the joints, and bring corruption upon the body in all its forms. By death the haughty are brought low, and the violent and hard-hearted are buried in its darkness...

10.19.8.en: O you greedy, who seize and plunder your fellows, remember death, and do not multiply your sins. For in that place sinners do not repent, and he who plundered the possessions of his companion does not even own his own money, but goes to the place where wealth is not used, and becomes nothing; his honor passes away, and his sins remain to stand against him on the day of judgment.

10.20.0.en: St. Aphrahat. "Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death" [21].

10.20.1.en: He sets death before his eyes, and asks for some rest, perhaps to prepare for departure, and so as not to sin, even in his thought, under the weight of trials. As the Psalmist says: "Lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death" (Ps 13:3). He asked for a time in which to return to himself, and asked for God's work in his life before he dies and the door is shut. "Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead?" (Ps 88:10)

10.20.2.en: Job does not ask for rest because he is attached to temporal life, for he knows that he is departing and will not return. "Before I go whence I shall not return."

10.20.3.en: Job presents to us a painful picture of death and the grave, such as prevailed even among believers before the Resurrection of Christ. "To the land of darkness and the shadow of death."

10.20.4.en: Job's appearance was a mockery to his friends and to those who passed by him; perhaps he longed for the grave, where there is darkness, so that no one would see his sores, and his body would decay like the rest of the bodies without distinction!

10.20.5.en: For us, our life is a constant battle, whose site is the land of the heart, the mind, and the senses; it is an inner war between light and darkness. The enemy of good will not rest until the last breath, reckoning himself a king with the right to possess all humanity under his authority. The believer by his departure declares his final victory, or the victory of the grace of God working in him.

10.20.6.en: * Many of our people die this (bodily) death, and so are freed from this world. This death, which (the people of the world) reckon a catastrophe, the servants of God regard as a departure to salvation.

10.20.7.en: The righteous die like the wicked, without distinction... but the righteous are called to rest, and the wicked to punishment.

10.20.8.en: Great peace is granted to the believers, and punishment to the unbelievers.

10.20.9.en: * As for rest, what do we find in the world but constant war with Satan, and struggle in a continual battle against his arrows and swords?! Our war is waged against love of money, pride, anger, and love of display, and our struggle is constant against the lusts of the flesh and the enticements of the world.

10.20.10.en: For man's mind is besieged by the enemy on every side, and the assaults of Satan close in upon it from every direction. With effort the mind is able to defend itself, and scarcely can it resist in every spot. If it disdains the love of money, the lusts rise up in it. If it overcomes the lusts, the love of display springs up. If it triumphs over the love of display, anger and pride are kindled in it, and drunkenness with wine entices it, and envy tears apart its agreement with others, and jealousy corrupts its friendships.

10.20.11.en: Thus the spirit suffers every day from many persecutions like these and from great dangers like these that distress the heart, and yet the heart still delights in remaining long here among the wars of Satan! Though it would have been more fitting for our longings and desires to be directed toward hastening to go to Christ by way of speedy death. For the Lord Himself taught us, saying: "Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy" (Jn 16:20).

10.20.12.en: Who among us does not wish to be without sorrow?!

10.20.13.en: Who among us does not long to hasten to obtain joy?!

10.20.14.en: The Lord Himself also declared the time of turning our sorrow into joy, saying: "But I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you" (Jn 16:22). Since our joy lies in seeing Christ... what blindness afflicts our mind, and what foolishness overtakes us, when we love the sorrows of the world and its afflictions and tears more than hastening toward the joy that will not be taken from us?!

10.21.0.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr. "A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness" [22].

10.21.1.en: St. John Chrysostom did not wish to speak about the location of Gehenna other than that it is "outside this world," but he spoke in some detail about its torments. In one of his homilies he says:

10.21.2.en: [It is a sea of fire, not a sea of the same kind with the dimensions we know here, but greater and fiercer, with waves of fire, strange and terrifying flames. There is there a great abyss filled with terrifying flame. One can see the fire coming out of it on every side like a ravenous beast...

10.21.3.en: There none can resist, none can escape.

10.21.4.en: There the gentle face of Christ, the giver of peace, is not seen anywhere.

10.21.5.en: And as those condemned to work in the mines are violent men, who no longer see their families but those who force them to labor, so it will be there. But it is not so simple as this, but far worse. For here a man can present a petition to the emperor asking for mercy, and the prisoner may be pardoned, but there this will not happen. They will not come out but will remain, enduring inexpressible torments.]

10.21.6.en: St. John Chrysostom says that in spite of all these torments, the chief torment of the condemned is their deprivation of the presence of the Lord and of the communion of the saints in heaven.

10.21.7.en: The degrees of torment in Hell differ, depending on the extent of man's sins, but all fall under them eternally.

10.21.8.en: He says: [It is impossible that the torments of Gehenna do not exist.] And he sees that these torments are not merely for the fulfillment of divine justice, but were established to urge humanity to repent and abstain from sin. He says: [If God is concerned that we not sin, and that we enter into such troubles for our correction, it is clear that He punishes sinners and crowns the righteous.] He also says that He prepared Gehenna so that no one would be cast into Gehenna.

10.21.9.en: * As outward death separates the body from the soul, so inward death separates the soul from God. Thus the "shadow of death" is the darkness of separation, in which each of those condemned by eternal fire that destroys him is in darkness with respect to the inner light.

10.21.10.en: Now the nature of fire is to give light, and it has the property of destroying; but the fire that is wrathful over former sins has the property of destroying and has no light. Therefore the Truth says to the perishing: "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels" (Mt 25:41). And as they are all represented in one person, He says: "Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness" (Mt 22:13).

10.21.11.en: If the fire that torments the perishing could have light, it would not have been said of those cast out, "cast him into darkness." Likewise the Psalmist says: "Fire has fallen upon them and they shall not behold the sun" (Ps 58:8) [Vulgate]. For the fire falls upon the wicked.

10.21.13.en: "Without any order": it seems to us that there is no particular order in the grave, but kings are equal with slaves, and the rich with the poor, etc.; each is buried in his turn as God appoints for him; but there is a precise divine plan concerning the chastenings that may come upon us, even if we cannot explain them.

10.21.14.en: * The words "without any order" are most remarkable, for Almighty God, who rightly punishes evils, will not allow even the torments to be "without order." The very punishments that proceed from the balance of justice cannot in any way be inflicted "without order"; for how could there be no order in the punishments He issues, since the punishment that overtakes those condemned eternally is according to the measure of the crime. As it is written: [But the powerful will have their torment more severe, and more severe torments come upon the strong] (Wis 6:6-7). It is said in the judgment of Babylon: "How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her" (Rev 18:7). If the punishment is according to the measure of the sin, it is an undeniable truth that there is an order preserved in the punishments...

10.21.15.en: As in our Father's house there are many mansions according to the diversity of the virtues, so there is a difference in crime, and the condemned are subjected to varied punishment in the fires of Gehenna. For although Gehenna is one and the same for all, this does not mean that all burn in the same manner.

10.21.16.en: * "And where the light is as darkness" [22]. Although the fire in that place gives no light for comfort, yet for the sake of their greater torment it shines with a certain purpose. For the condemned will see by the shining flame their followers with them in torment, those who, for love of the disobedient, preferred the love of fleshly life to the commandments of the Creator...

10.21.17.en: The Truth shows us that the rich man, whose lot it was to go down into the torments of eternal fire (Lk 17:19-31), is described as remembering his five brothers, and he asked Abraham to send to them to teach them, lest they fall under the same punishment in the future. It is clear without doubt that he who remembers his absent relatives has multiplied his own pains; how much more, when afterward he sees them with his own eyes present with him, does it increase his torment.

10.21.19.en: * On the day of judgment, there is no doubt that the good will be separated from the bad, and the righteous from the wicked. And to every soul, through the judgment of God, will be assigned a place befitting its worthiness and merit, God willing.

10.21.20.en: Origen. * We speak of many degrees and various measures in both the Kingdom and Gehenna... For God, as a just judge, gives each one according to the measure of his faith.

10.21.21.en: * In the light and in the glory there are degrees. And in Gehenna itself and in the punishment it appears that there are sorcerers and thieves, as there are others who committed lesser sins.

10.21.24.en: * When afflictions hem me in, I feel bitterness and distress.

10.21.25.en: I loathe my life, longing for death.

10.21.26.en: Anxiety fills my depths, and my whole inner being trembles.

10.21.27.en: I cry out with Job: My soul is weary of my life.

10.21.28.en: Truly, in my weakness I have often longed for death.

10.21.29.en: I have often wondered why You created me.

10.21.30.en: But when I lift my eyes to You, in the midst of my trials I will not forget that I am the work of Your hands.

10.21.31.en: In the midst of my chastenings I will not ignore Your constant care for me.

10.21.32.en: You are love, wholly wisdom and wholly fatherhood and love!

10.21.33.en: I look to You, and You carry me in the midst of my chastenings into Your embrace.

10.21.34.en: I remember Your fatherhood, and I forget all my troubles.

10.21.35.en: Truly I perceive my hidden sins; instead of thinking about the affliction, my soul is distressed by my iniquities.

10.21.36.en: Instead of longing for death, I seek Your grace that forgives sins.

10.21.37.en: Instead of murmuring, I condemn myself.

10.21.38.en: I confess my sins now, that You may cover me on the day of judgment.

10.21.39.en: I am exposed before myself, so that I may be covered by Your righteousness.

10.21.40.en: Affliction turns into peace, as I hide in You and take refuge in You, O refuge of my life.

10.21.41.en: Instead of the weight of afflictions that crushes the soul, I enjoy the weight of eternal glory that lifts my soul to heavenly things.

10.21.42.en: I forget all pain, and even long for it, for it is the way of fellowship with You in the Cross, as in the glory of the Resurrection.

10.21.43.en: * In my affliction and in the midst of my pains I realize that I am a sinner.

10.21.44.en: But I need Your Holy Spirit to enlighten my insight, that I may know my sin and discover it, and so confess it to You.

10.21.45.en: I hate it, and cry out to You that Your grace may support me, and I may flee from it.

10.21.46.en: Who exposes my soul before me but Your light, O Lord.

10.21.47.en: Let it shine upon me, that I may perceive my weaknesses, and with rejoicing hope for the riches of Your love that forgives all my sins!

10.21.48.en: Grant me to judge myself here, so that You may not pass judgment on me on the day of Your coming!

10.21.49.en: * In my weakness sufferings swallowed my soul; I reckoned that You had left the wicked to destroy me.

10.21.50.en: But when I lift my eyes to You, I realize that You did not permit me affliction beyond my endurance.

10.21.51.en: In Your love You set limits to affliction, and it does not exceed them.

10.21.52.en: And by Your grace You grant me the gift of joyful endurance, and pour upon me the fruit of the Spirit, patience, a way of passing over into the glories.

10.21.53.en: Truly You do not leave the rod of the wicked to rest upon the righteous.

10.21.54.en: Rather through it You prove them, and bring them over into eternity.

10.21.55.en: * My God, You know my depths, You are the Creator of time, and You are above time.

10.21.56.en: You have no need to examine me by trials.

10.21.57.en: For in my weakness I fear the pressures of the enemy upon me.

10.21.58.en: Lest he turn me aside to evil!

10.21.59.en: I flee to You that You may keep me from him!

10.21.60.en: * My God, I confess to You that I am a sinner.

10.21.61.en: By Your grace I cry out with the Apostle Peter:

10.21.62.en: You know, Lord, that I love You.

10.21.63.en: I do not want to resist You, nor to disobey You.

10.21.64.en: But this will not justify me, for I am weak.

10.21.65.en: Support me by Your grace, that I may bear Your righteousness.

10.21.66.en: * Truly I groan because of my body, yet it is the work of Your good hands.

10.21.67.en: Scatter the corruption that has crept into it, and sanctify the body that You created and wish to glorify!

10.21.68.en: You, the eternal Word, became flesh, that by Your incarnation You might sanctify my whole being.

10.21.69.en: So I do not belittle the body, for it is a partner of the soul in glory!

10.21.70.en: Glory to You, who honor our bodies in Yourself!

10.21.71.en: You have honored my body, because it is the work of Your hands!

10.21.72.en: And when I dishonored it by my sins, You became incarnate to glorify what You created!

10.21.73.en: * I am the work of Your hands, You cherish me!

10.21.74.en: I am confident of Your surpassing providence, however the waves rise against me.

10.21.75.en: But my mind remains in its weakness, unable to comprehend Your wisdom!

10.21.76.en: Reveal to me the mystery of Your love, that I may not stumble!

10.21.77.en: Make known to me Your judgments, that I may meditate in Your love!

10.21.78.en: * You are wonderful in Your care for me, for if I sin You watch me, lest I turn aside further; You lead me with the rod of discipline, that I may not fall into the den of wolves.

10.21.79.en: You draw me with a love full of firmness, and a firmness full of gentleness!

10.21.80.en: * Quickly I look to Your Cross, and pass over with You to Your tomb, O my Savior.

10.21.81.en: So death becomes for me not out of despair and despondency, but a fellowship of love with Him who died for me; indeed I long to die with You, out of love for You and for those You love.

10.21.82.en: I no longer look to the years of my life, but I await the salvation of the whole world!

10.21.83.en: I do not fear events, but rejoice in the salvation of many!

10.21.84.en: You are wonderful in Your love, You who turn even death into a joyful gift!

10.21.85.en: * I will no longer be preoccupied with my afflictions.

10.21.86.en: I will no longer cry out in folly, saying:

10.21.87.en: Lift Your hand from me, for I have sunk in the midst of my bitterness. I will not cry out to You as a fool, reckoning that death is a rest for me from my toils.

10.21.88.en: * Rise, O Sun of righteousness, upon me and upon humanity, and scatter the darkness of our thoughts, and bring us out of our inner graves, and turn our dry bones into an exceeding great army.

10.21.89.en: Let me enjoy with Ezekiel the vision of the resurrection of humanity in You (Ezek 38).

10.21.90.en: So there will be no darkness in my life, and I will no longer suffer from night!

10.21.91.en: But in Your light I will perceive the mysteries of Your salvation, and enjoy the delight of knowing Your wonderful dispensation.

10.21.92.en: And I will be always a son of light, and a son of the day!
